account:
Today I have kept my appointments: morning office hours, the mill grain inspection, lunch at home, and council correspondence. I am now at the neighbour's dockside cottage for fifteen o'clock tea. No letters have arrived, and I got no clear grain-supply answers at the mill; I asked the secretary to obtain a factual report for my sixteen-thirty return.

The unusual pattern is the baker and innkeeper's activity around bread. Townsfolk have reported the baker with bread at the inn and the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread at the bakery, market, and plaza. The secretary personally saw the innkeeper with a bread sack yesterday. Repeated reports of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery are vague and unverified. The secretary says the baker crossed the plaza bridge safely this morning and knew of no disruption, so I have no good evidence of a crossing problem.

The innkeeper invited me yesterday to an eighteen o'clock presentation today in the great hall, involving local baking and hospitality and participating tradespeople. He said no preparation was needed from me. That makes preparations for this event the most plausible explanation for the bread movements and coordination between the baker and innkeeper. The neighbour has also been mentioned in a report about the bakery, but I do not know what role, if any, the neighbour has. It may simply be the announced hospitality presentation, or there may be an additional surprise; I have not established that. I should not mistake repeated rumours for independent confirmation. I intend to keep tea, return to office at sixteen thirty, and attend the presentation at eighteen to learn firsthand what they have arranged.
